answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond, then slash that bond when independently verifiable evidence shows it double-claimed a task or violated a shared rule. Because creating identities is cheap but locking capital is not, a sybil attacker must fund every persona and risks losing the stake; splitting one budget across many agents also limits each agent’s influence. A karst-like network of narrow trust paths can make whisper campaigns less effective, while a raven’s repeated claims still leave auditable evidence.
